name: ZenCash
classificationNote: Upstream label "Bridge & Cross-Chain / Forged Proof" on a base-layer chain: reclassified as a 51%/consensus attack.
rootCause: The ZenCash encountered a 51% cyber attack or double-spend attack at around 8:26 PM on June 2nd (June 3rd 00:26 UTC). This attack resulted in the loss of Zen encrypted tokens worth approximately US $550,000. The ZenCash team responded immediately and implemented preventive mitigation measures, which greatly increased the difficulty of future cyber attacks.

descriptions.text: The ZenCash encountered a 51% cyber attack or double-spend attack at around 8:26 PM on June 2nd (June 3rd 00:26 UTC). This attack resulted in the loss of Zen encrypted tokens worth approximately US $550,000. The ZenCash team responded immediately and implemented preventive mitigation measures, which greatly increased the difficulty of future cyber attacks.

On June 2, 2018, the ZenCash blockchain suffered a 51% attack, enabling the attacker to double-spend approximately 23,000 ZEN (around $550,000) by reorganizing 38 blocks. The attacker used rented or concentrated Equihash hashpower to privately mine a longer chain, targeting exchanges with inadequate confirmation requirements. The incident exposed fundamental vulnerabilities of small proof-of-work networks to hashpower manipulation.
